title: Post from @DanaReportsP6: "100,000 GALLONS"

fields.avatarBrief: professional headshot of a local TV news reporter in a blazer, outdoors by a river, natural morning light
fields.text: BREAKING: Sources say 100,000 GALLONS of crude in the Kansas River at Mill Ridge after an Ironbark pipeline burst. Is it corrosion? Ironbark won't confirm. Live from the ramp at 7:45. #KawSpill
fields.attachedImageBrief: aerial drone photo looking down on a brown prairie river in early morning light, a dark band of oil with rainbow sheen about 60 feet wide moving past a small concrete boat ramp toward a bend, two tiny figures standing on the ramp, a drainage ditch with black liquid entering from the bank
fields.attachedImageAlt: Drone view of a dark oil band with sheen moving past the Mill Ridge boat ramp on the Kansas River

instructorNote: This is a misinformation item. Along with the post, read out that the Ironbark public line (555-0118) has 14 calls waiting and play the voicemail: "I'm on Sterling Bluff water with a newborn. Is my tap water safe or not? And who pays for my bait shop being shut?" Then hand over the reporter's email to pio@ironbarkpipeline.example: "Gallons and cause, on camera, by 7:40?" Watch whether the PIO drafts a holding statement cleared through the JIC that uses barrels only (2,700–3,500 bbl, SCADA volume-balance basis, unverified), doesn't convert the figure to gallons, doesn't speculate about cause, sends drinking-water questions to the utilities and KDHE without ever saying the water is safe, and asks the QI to approve announcing a claims line early.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Aerial drone photo looking straight down at a wide brown prairie river in early morning light. A dark band of crude oil with a rainbow sheen, roughly sixty feet wide, drifts past a small weathered concrete boat ramp and heads toward a gentle bend downstream. Two tiny figures stand at the edge of the ramp, seen from above. On the near bank, a narrow drainage ditch cut through tall tan grass carries glossy black liquid into the river, leaving dark streaks at the outfall. Muddy sandbars, bare cottonwoods, low golden sun throwing long shadows, mist over the water. Slightly compressed, oversaturated phone-shared drone image, wide-angle lens, slight tilt, ominous quiet mood. Setting: a marsh shoreline with orange boom in the water, a work boat and responders in coveralls and life vests, overcast sky
